title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 212: Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 212 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Cracking the Code: The Decipherment of Linear B

Paragraph 1. In the spring of 1900, British archaeologist Arthur Evans started digging on the island of Crete. He quickly uncovered the huge ruins of an ancient palace. Inside the rooms, Evans found thousands of small clay tablets covered with strange lines. He named the older writing Linear A and the younger writing Linear B. Evans strongly believed that Linear B had no connection to the Greek language.

Paragraph 2. The soft clay notes only lasted for thousands of years because big fires burned the palace and baked the clay into hard stone. For more than forty years, nobody could read Linear B. Experts did not have a two-language key like Egypt's famous Rosetta Stone. Sadly, Arthur Evans died in 1941 without reading even one sentence.

Paragraph 3. The big step forward came from a quiet American teacher named Alice Kober. During World War II, paper was scarce, so Kober cut little study cards out of old exam sheets. She carefully sorted thousands of symbols and noticed changing word endings. Before dying in 1950, she drew a smart sound chart showing how consonants joined vowels.

Paragraph 4. In 1952, young British architect Michael Ventris used Kober's chart to test town names in Crete. Suddenly, Greek words appeared! Ventris proved Linear B was actually an early form of Greek, written five hundred years before Homer. The tablets were not poems; they were tax lists counting olive oil, grain, and sheep.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 1: "...uncovered the huge ruins of an ancient palace."
Đoạn 2: "...because big fires burned the palace and baked the clay..."
Đoạn 3: "During World War II, paper was scarce..."
Đoạn 4: "...tax lists counting olive oil, grain, and sheep."

q5.text: What did Arthur Evans believe about the language on Linear B tablets?
options: A. It was written by Roman soldiers.
B. It was an early version of English.
C. It had no link to the Greek language.
D. It was identical to Egyptian writing.

steps: Đoạn 1: "Evans strongly believed that Linear B had no connection to the Greek language."

q6.text: How did the clay tablets survive for thousands of years?
options: A. Fires baked the soft clay into hard material.
B. Workers covered every tablet with thick oil.
C. They were buried inside dry mountain caves.
D. Kings kept them locked inside metal boxes.

steps: Đoạn 2: Các trận hỏa hoạn làm đất sét nung cứng như đá nên mới tồn tại lâu.

q7.text: Why did Alice Kober make study cards out of old exam sheets?
options: A. She wanted to copy her students' test answers.
B. Old exams already had Linear B symbols on them.
C. She preferred writing on coloured paper.
D. Normal paper was very hard to find during the war.

steps: Đoạn 3: Trong Thế chiến II, giấy rất khan hiếm (paper was scarce).

q8.text: What did the translated Linear B tablets actually contain?
options: A. Famous adventure poems about sea gods
B. Tax lists recording food and farm animals
C. Secret peace agreements between kings
D. Personal letters written by palace guards

steps: Đoạn 4: Đó là các bảng kê khai thuế đếm dầu ô-liu, ngũ cốc và cừu.
